title: Flags on Red Cells
text: If you have type A blood, your red cells carry A flags, and your plasma naturally contains antibodies against B.
nxt: If you have type B, the reverse is true. Type AB cells carry both flags, so the immune system attacks neither.

title: The Bombay Puzzle
text: The mystery pushed scientists to look at how the flags are built. The A and B antigens do not attach straight to the cell.

title: The Bombay Puzzle
text: They are built on a base molecule called the H antigen, like a flagpole planted in the cell surface.
nxt: Enzymes add one sugar to that pole to make an A flag, or a different sugar to make a B flag.

title: The Rh Factor
text: Bombay blood is not the only unusual profile. To meet the next one, look at the small plus or minus sign after your blood type.

title: The Rh Factor
text: That sign belongs to the Rh system, named after the rhesus monkeys whose blood was used in experiments in 1940.
nxt: Most people think of Rh as a simple switch: positive or negative. The truth is far richer.
